115	        object.__setattr__(self, "columns", cols)
116	
117	    @property
118	    def names(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
119	        return tuple(col.name for col in self.columns)
120	
121	    def index(self, name: str) -> int:
122	        for i, col in enumerate(self.columns):
123	            if col.name == name:
124	                return i
125	        raise KeyError(name)
126	
127	
128	class Table:
129	    """A schema together with equal-length, column-oriented Python lists."""
130	
131	    def __init__(self, schema: Schema, columns: Mapping[str, Sequence] | Sequence[Sequence]):
132	        if not isinstance(schema, Schema):
133	            raise TypeError("schema must be a Schema instance")
134	        aligned = _align_columns(schema, columns)
135	        row_count = _validate_columns(schema, aligned)
136	        self.schema = schema
137	        self._row_count = row_count
138	        self._columns = tuple(tuple(col) for col in aligned)
139	
140	    @classmethod
141	    def _from_storage(cls, schema: Schema, columns: Sequence[Sequence]) -> "Table":
142	        """Build without re-validating (used by the decoder)."""
143	        obj = cls.__new__(cls)
144	        obj.schema = schema
145	        obj._row_count = len(columns[0]) if columns else 0
146	        obj._columns = tuple(tuple(col) for col in columns)
147	        return obj
148	
149	    @property
150	    def row_count(self) -> int:
151	        return self._row_count
152	
153	    @property
154	    def column_names(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
155	        return self.schema.names
156	
157	    def column(self, name: str) -> list:
158	        """Return a fresh list of the named column's values."""
159	        return list(self._columns[self.schema.index(name)])
160	
161	    @property
162	    def columns(self) -> dict[str, list]:
163	        """Column name to value list, in schema order."""
164	        return {name: list(self._columns[i]) for i, name in enumerate(self.schema.names)}
165	
166	    def project(self, names: Sequence[str]) -> "Table":
167	        """Return a table restricted to ``names``, in the requested order.
168	
169	        Unknown names raise :class:`KeyError`; repeated names raise
170	        :class:`ValueError`.
171	        """
172	        if isinstance(names, str):
173	            raise ValueError("project names must be a sequence of strings, not a single string")
174	        requested = tuple(names)
175	        if len(set(requested)) != len(requested):
176	            raise ValueError("projection contains duplicate column names")
177	        indices = []
178	        for name in requested:
179	            indices.append(self.schema.index(name))  # KeyError on unknown name
180	        sub_schema = Schema([self.schema.columns[i] for i in indices])
181	        sub_cols = [self._columns[i] for i in indices]
182	        return Table._from_storage(sub_schema, sub_cols)
183	
184	
185	def _align_columns(
186	    schema: Schema, columns: Mapping[str, Sequence] | Sequence[Sequence]
187	) -> list[Sequence]:
188	    if isinstance(columns, Mapping):
189	        missing = [name for name in schema.names if name not in columns]
190	        if missing:
191	            raise ValueError(f"missing column(s): {', '.join(missing)!r}")
192	        extra = [name for name in columns if name not in set(schema.names)]
193	        if extra:
194	            raise ValueError(f"unexpected column(s): {', '.join(map(str, extra))!r}")
195	        return [columns[name] for name in schema.names]
196	    if isinstance(columns, Sequence) and not isinstance(columns, (str, bytes)):
197	        if len(columns) != len(schema.columns):
198	            raise ValueError(
199	                f"expected {len(schema.columns)} columns, got {len(columns)}"
200	            )
201	        return list(columns)
202	    raise TypeError("columns must be a mapping or a sequence aligned to the schema")
203	
204	
205	def _validate_columns(schema: Schema, columns: Sequence[Sequence]) -> int:
206	    """Check shape, nullability, per-value Python types and float finiteness."""
207	    row_count: int | None = None
208	    for col, raw in zip(schema.columns, columns):
209	        try:
210	            values = list(raw)
211	        except TypeError:
212	            raise ValueError(f"column {col.name!r} is not a sequence") from None
213	        if row_count is None:
214	            row_count = len(values)
215	        elif len(values) != row_count:
216	            raise ValueError(
217	                f"column {col.name!r} has {len(values)} rows, expected {row_count}"
218	            )
219	        for position, value in enumerate(values):
220	            where = f"column {col.name!r} row {position}"
221	            if value is None:
222	                if not col.nullable:
223	                    raise ValueError(f"{where}: NULL in non-nullable column")
224	                continue
225	            if col.type == "bool":
226	                if not isinstance(value, bool):
227	                    raise ValueError(f"{where}: expected bool, got {type(value).__name__}")
228	            elif col.type == "int64":
229	                if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
230	                    raise ValueError(f"{where}: expected int64, got {type(value).__name__}")
231	                if not (-(2**63) <= value <= 2**63 - 1):
232	                    raise ValueError(f"{where}: value outside int64 range")
233	            elif col.type == "float64":
234	                if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, float):
235	                    raise ValueError(f"{where}: expected float64, got {type(value).__name__}")

254	def _pack_bits(flags: Sequence[bool]) -> bytes:
255	    out = bytearray((len(flags) + 7) // 8)
256	    for i, flag in enumerate(flags):
257	        if flag:
258	            out[i >> 3] |= 1 << (i & 7)
259	    return bytes(out)

262	def _check_padding(bits: bytes, count: int, what: str) -> None:
263	    if count % 8:
264	        unused = bits[-1] >> (count % 8)
265	        if unused:
266	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"non-zero padding bits in {what}")

269	def _encode_payload(
270	    col: ColumnSchema, values: Sequence, use_dictionary: bool
271	) -> tuple[bytes, int, Any, Any]:
272	    n = len(values)
273	    null_count = 0
274	    minimum: Any = None
275	    maximum: Any = None
276	    validity = bytearray((n + 7) // 8) if col.nullable else None

278	    if col.type == "bool":
279	        flags: list[bool] = []
280	        for i, value in enumerate(values):
281	            if value is None:
282	                flags.append(False)
283	                null_count += 1
284	                continue
285	            if validity is not None:
286	                validity[i >> 3] |= 1 << (i & 7)
287	            flags.append(value)
288	            if minimum is None or value < minimum:
289	                minimum = value
290	            if maximum is None or value > maximum:
291	                maximum = value
292	        body = _pack_bits(flags)
293	    elif col.type == "int64":
294	        buf = bytearray()
295	        for i, value in enumerate(values):
296	            if value is None:
297	                buf.extend(b"\x00" * 8)
298	                null_count += 1
299	                continue
300	            if validity is not None:
301	                validity[i >> 3] |= 1 << (i & 7)

303	            if minimum is None or value < minimum:
304	                minimum = value
305	            if maximum is None or value > maximum:
306	                maximum = value
307	        body = bytes(buf)
308	    elif col.type == "float64":
309	        buf = bytearray()
310	        for i, value in enumerate(values):
311	            if value is None:
312	                buf.extend(b"\x00" * 8)
313	                null_count += 1
314	                continue
315	            if validity is not None:
316	                validity[i >> 3] |= 1 << (i & 7)
317	            buf.extend(struct.pack("<d", value))
318	            if minimum is None or value < minimum:
319	                minimum = value
320	            if maximum is None or value > maximum:
321	                maximum = value
322	        body = bytes(buf)
323	    else:  # utf8

325	            dictionary: list[str] = []
326	            dictionary_index: dict[str, int] = {}

328	            for i, value in enumerate(values):
329	                if value is None:
330	                    indices.extend(struct.pack("<i", -1))
331	                    null_count += 1
332	                    continue
333	                if validity is not None:
334	                    validity[i >> 3] |= 1 << (i & 7)
335	                idx = dictionary_index.get(value)
336	                if idx is None:
337	                    # Dictionary ids follow first-occurrence order.
338	                    idx = len(dictionary)
339	                    dictionary_index[value] = idx
340	                    dictionary.append(value)
341	                indices.extend(struct.pack("<i", idx))
342	                if minimum is None or value < minimum:
343	                    minimum = value
344	                if maximum is None or value > maximum:
345	                    maximum = value
346	            body = (
347	                struct.pack("<I", len(dictionary))
348	                + _encode_utf8_strings(dictionary)
349	                + bytes(indices)
350	            )
351	        else:
352	            ordered: list[str] = []
353	            for i, value in enumerate(values):
354	                if value is None:
355	                    ordered.append("")
356	                    null_count += 1
357	                    continue
358	                if validity is not None:
359	                    validity[i >> 3] |= 1 << (i & 7)
360	                ordered.append(value)
361	                if minimum is None or value < minimum:
362	                    minimum = value
363	                if maximum is None or value > maximum:
364	                    maximum = value
365	            body = _encode_utf8_strings(ordered)
366	
367	    payload = (bytes(validity) if validity is not None else b"") + body
368	    return payload, null_count, minimum, maximum

370	
371	def _encode_utf8_strings(strings: Sequence[str]) -> bytes:
372	    offsets = bytearray()
373	    blob = bytearray()
374	    cursor = 0
375	    offsets.extend(struct.pack("<I", 0))
376	    for value in strings:
377	        raw = value.encode("utf-8")
378	        cursor += len(raw)
379	        blob.extend(raw)
380	        offsets.extend(struct.pack("<I", cursor))
381	    return bytes(offsets) + bytes(blob)

384	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
385	# Decoding
386	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
387	
388	
389	def _decode_column(
390	    col: ColumnSchema, encoding: str, row_count: int, payload: bytes
391	) -> list:
392	    cursor = 0
393	    validity: bytes | None = None
394	    if col.nullable:
395	        size = (row_count + 7) // 8
396	        if len(payload) < cursor + size:
397	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"truncated validity bitmap for {col.name!r}")
398	        validity = payload[cursor : cursor + size]
399	        _check_padding(validity, row_count, f"validity bitmap of {col.name!r}")
400	        cursor += size
401	    body = payload[cursor:]
402	
403	    if col.type == "bool":
404	        size = (row_count + 7) // 8
405	        if len(body) != size:
406	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"bad bool payload length for {col.name!r}")
407	        _check_padding(body, row_count, f"bool payload of {col.name!r}")
408	        values = [
409	            bool((body[i >> 3] >> (i & 7)) & 1) for i in range(row_count)
410	        ]
411	    elif col.type == "int64":
412	        if len(body) != 8 * row_count:
413	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"bad int64 payload length for {col.name!r}")
414	        values = list(struct.unpack(f"<{row_count}q", body)) if row_count else []
415	    elif col.type == "float64":
416	        if len(body) != 8 * row_count:
417	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"bad float64 payload length for {col.name!r}")
418	        values = list(struct.unpack(f"<{row_count}d", body)) if row_count else []
419	        for i, value in enumerate(values):
420	            if value != value or value in (float("inf"), float("-inf")):
421	                raise ColumnarFormatError(
422	                    f"non-finite float64 stored in {col.name!r} row {i}"
423	                )
424	    elif encoding == "dictionary":
425	        values = _decode_dict_utf8(col, row_count, body, validity)
426	    else:
427	        values = _decode_plain_utf8(col, row_count, body)
428	
429	    if validity is not None:
430	        for i in range(row_count):
431	            if not ((validity[i >> 3] >> (i & 7)) & 1):
432	                values[i] = None
433	    return values
434	
435	
436	def _decode_utf8_blob(col: ColumnSchema, body: bytes, count: int, *, what: str) -> list[str]:
437	    offset_bytes = 4 * (count + 1)
438	    if len(body) < offset_bytes:
439	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"truncated {what} offsets for {col.name!r}")
440	    offsets = struct.unpack(f"<{count + 1}I", body[:offset_bytes])
441	    blob = body[offset_bytes:]
442	    if offsets[0] != 0:
443	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"{what} offsets must start at 0 for {col.name!r}")
444	    for prev, nxt in zip(offsets, offsets[1:]):
445	        if nxt < prev:
446	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"non-monotonic {what} offsets for {col.name!r}")
447	    if offsets[-1] != len(blob):
448	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"{what} byte length mismatch for {col.name!r}")
449	    strings = []
450	    for i in range(count):
451	        raw = blob[offsets[i] : offsets[i + 1]]
452	        try:
453	            strings.append(raw.decode("utf-8"))
454	        except UnicodeDecodeError:
455	            raise ColumnarFormatError(
456	                f"invalid UTF-8 in {what} entry {i} of {col.name!r}"
457	            ) from None
458	    return strings
459	
460	
461	def _decode_plain_utf8(col: ColumnSchema, row_count: int, body: bytes) -> list[str]:
462	    return _decode_utf8_blob(col, body, row_count, what="utf8")
463	
464	
465	def _decode_dict_utf8(
466	    col: ColumnSchema, row_count: int, body: bytes, validity: bytes | None
467	) -> list[str]:
468	    if len(body) < 4:
469	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"truncated dictionary header for {col.name!r}")
470	    (dict_size,) = struct.unpack("<I", body[:4])
471	    rest = body[4:]
472	    offset_bytes = 4 * (dict_size + 1)
473	    # Split dictionary section from the trailing row indices.
474	    if len(rest) < offset_bytes:
475	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"truncated dictionary offsets for {col.name!r}")
476	    tentative_offsets = struct.unpack(f"<{dict_size + 1}I", rest[:offset_bytes])
477	    dict_section_len = offset_bytes + tentative_offsets[-1]
478	    if dict_section_len > len(rest) - 4 * row_count:
479	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"dictionary overruns payload for {col.name!r}")
480	    dictionary = _decode_utf8_blob(
481	        col, rest[:dict_section_len], dict_size, what="dictionary"
482	    )
483	    index_bytes = rest[dict_section_len:]
484	    if len(index_bytes) != 4 * row_count:
485	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"bad dictionary index length for {col.name!r}")
486	    raw_indices = struct.unpack(f"<{row_count}i", index_bytes) if row_count else ()
487	    values: list[str] = []
488	    for i, idx in enumerate(raw_indices):
489	        is_valid = validity is None or bool((validity[i >> 3] >> (i & 7)) & 1)
490	        if idx == -1:
491	            if not col.nullable or is_valid:
492	                raise ColumnarFormatError(
493	                    f"NULL dictionary index contradicts validity in {col.name!r} row {i}"
494	                )
495	            values.append("")  # replaced with None via validity bitmap below
496	        elif not 0 <= idx < dict_size:
497	            raise ColumnarFormatError(
498	                f"dictionary index {idx} out of range in {col.name!r} row {i}"
499	            )
500	        else:
501	            if not is_valid:
502	                raise ColumnarFormatError(
503	                    f"valid dictionary index in NULL slot of {col.name!r} row {i}"
504	                )
505	            values.append(dictionary[idx])
506	    return values
507

514	def _stats_json(value: Any) -> Any:
515	    return value

517	
518	def _build_header(
519	    table: Table,
520	    compression: str,
521	    data_section: bytes,
522	    raw_section: bytes,
523	    chunk_info: Sequence[dict],
524	) -> dict:
525	    return {
526	        "compression": compression,
527	        "row_count": table.row_count,
528	        "data_length": len(data_section),
529	        "data_crc32": zlib.crc32(data_section) & 0xFFFFFFFF,
530	        "uncompressed_length": len(raw_section),
531	        "columns": list(chunk_info),
532	    }

534	
535	def _dump_json(header: dict) -> bytes:
536	    return json.dumps(
537	        header, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False
538	    ).encode("utf-8")
539	
540	
541	def _reject_duplicate_keys(pairs: Sequence[tuple[str, Any]]) -> dict:
542	    seen: set[str] = set()
543	    for key, _ in pairs:
544	        if key in seen:
545	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"duplicate JSON key in header: {key!r}")
546	        seen.add(key)
547	    return dict(pairs)
548	
549	
550	def _reject_json_constant(value: str):
551	    raise ColumnarFormatError(f"illegal JSON constant in header: {value}")
552	
553	
554	def _is_uint32(value: Any) -> bool:
555	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and 0 <= value <= 0xFFFFFFFF
556	
557	
558	def _is_nonneg_int(value: Any) -> bool:
559	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value >= 0
560	
561	
562	def _validate_header(header: Any) -> dict:
563	    if not isinstance(header, dict):
564	        raise ColumnarFormatError("header must be a JSON object")
565	    unknown = set(header) - _HEADER_KEYS
566	    if unknown:
567	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"unknown header key(s): {sorted(unknown)!r}")
568	    compression = header.get("compression")
569	    if compression not in _COMPRESSION_NAMES:
570	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"unknown compression in header: {compression!r}")
571	    row_count = header.get("row_count")
572	    if not _is_nonneg_int(row_count):
573	        raise ColumnarFormatError("header row_count must be a non-negative integer")
574	    data_length = header.get("data_length")
575	    if not _is_nonneg_int(data_length):
576	        raise ColumnarFormatError("header data_length must be a non-negative integer")
577	    data_crc = header.get("data_crc32")
578	    if not _is_uint32(data_crc):
579	        raise ColumnarFormatError("header data_crc32 must be a uint32")
580	    uncompressed_length = header.get("uncompressed_length")
581	    if not _is_nonneg_int(uncompressed_length):
582	        raise ColumnarFormatError("header uncompressed_length must be a non-negative integer")
583	    entries = header.get("columns")
584	    if not isinstance(entries, list) or not entries:
585	        raise ColumnarFormatError("header must list at least one column")
586	
587	    seen: set[str] = set()
588	    next_offset = 0
589	    for pos, entry in enumerate(entries):
590	        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
591	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column header #{pos} must be an object")
592	        unknown_col = set(entry) - _COLUMN_KEYS
593	        if unknown_col:
594	            raise ColumnarFormatError(
595	                f"column header #{pos}: unknown key(s) {sorted(unknown_col)!r}"
596	            )
597	        name = entry.get("name")
598	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
599	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column header #{pos}: name must be a non-empty string")
600	        if name in seen:
601	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"duplicate column in header: {name!r}")
602	        seen.add(name)
603	        col_type = entry.get("type")
604	        if col_type not in _TYPE_NAMES:
605	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: unknown type {col_type!r}")
606	        nullable = entry.get("nullable")
607	        if not isinstance(nullable, bool):
608	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: nullable must be true or false")
609	        encoding = entry.get("encoding")
610	        if encoding not in _ENCODING_NAMES:
611	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: unknown encoding {encoding!r}")
612	        if encoding == "dictionary" and col_type != "utf8":
613	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: dictionary encoding requires utf8")
614	        for key in ("offset", "length", "null_count"):
615	            if not _is_nonneg_int(entry.get(key)):
616	                raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: {key} must be a non-negative integer")
617	        if not _is_uint32(entry.get("crc32")):
618	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: crc32 must be a uint32")
619	        if "min" not in entry or "max" not in entry:
620	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: min and max keys are required")
621	        if entry["offset"] != next_offset:
622	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: chunks are not contiguous")
623	        next_offset += entry["length"]
624	        null_count = entry["null_count"]
625	        if null_count > row_count:
626	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: null_count exceeds row_count")
627	        if not nullable and null_count:
628	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: NULL count set for non-nullable column")
629	        _validate_stats(entry, col_type, row_count, null_count)
630	    if next_offset != uncompressed_length:
631	        raise ColumnarFormatError("declared uncompressed length does not match column chunks")
632	    return header
633	
634	
635	def _validate_stats(
636	    entry: dict, col_type: str, row_count: int, null_count: int
637	) -> None:
638	    name = entry["name"]
639	    minimum = entry.get("min")
640	    maximum = entry.get("max")
641	    if null_count == row_count:
642	        if minimum is not None or maximum is not None:
643	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: all-NULL column needs null min/max")
644	        return
645	    if minimum is None or maximum is None:
646	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: min and max must both be present")
647	    if col_type == "bool":
648	        if not isinstance(minimum, bool) or not isinstance(maximum, bool):
649	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: bool stats must be booleans")
650	    elif col_type == "int64":
651	        if not _is_int64_json(minimum) or not _is_int64_json(maximum):
652	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: int64 stats must be int64 integers")
653	    elif col_type == "float64":
654	        if not _is_finite_json_float(minimum) or not _is_finite_json_float(maximum):
655	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: float64 stats must be finite numbers")
656	        minimum = float(minimum)
657	        maximum = float(maximum)
658	    elif col_type == "utf8":
659	        if not isinstance(minimum, str) or not isinstance(maximum, str):
660	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: utf8 stats must be strings")
661	    if minimum > maximum:
662	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {name!r}: min exceeds max")
663	
664	
665	def _is_int64_json(value: Any) -> bool:
666	    return (
667	        isinstance(value, int)
668	        and not isinstance(value, bool)
669	        and -(2**63) <= value <= 2**63 - 1
670	    )
671	
672	
673	def _is_finite_json_float(value: Any) -> bool:
674	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
675	        return False
676	    value = float(value)
677	    return value == value and value not in (float("inf"), float("-inf"))
678

681	# Writing
682	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
683	
684	
685	def write_file(
686	    path: str | os.PathLike,
687	    table: Table,
688	    *,
689	    compression: str = "none",
690	    dictionary_encoding: Sequence[str] = (),
691	) -> None:
692	    """Write ``table`` to ``path`` deterministically and atomically.
693	
694	    All validation happens before any file is created, so invalid arguments
695	    never create or alter the destination.
696	    """
697	    if not isinstance(table, Table):
698	        raise TypeError("table must be a Table instance")
699	    if compression not in _COMPRESSION_NAMES:
700	        raise ValueError(f"unknown compression: {compression!r}")
701	    if isinstance(dictionary_encoding, str):
702	        raise ValueError("dictionary_encoding must be a sequence of column names")
703	    dict_names = tuple(dictionary_encoding)
704	    if len(set(dict_names)) != len(dict_names):
705	        raise ValueError("dictionary_encoding contains duplicate column names")
706	    unknown = [name for name in dict_names if name not in table.schema.names]
707	    if unknown:
708	        raise ValueError(f"dictionary_encoding references unknown column(s): {unknown!r}")
709	    for name in dict_names:
710	        col = table.schema.columns[table.schema.index(name)]
711	        if col.type != "utf8":
712	            raise ValueError(
713	                f"dictionary encoding is only valid for utf8 columns, not {col.name!r} ({col.type})"
714	            )
715	    dict_set = set(dict_names)
716	
717	    raw_section = bytearray()
718	    chunk_info: list[dict] = []
719	    for i, col in enumerate(table.schema.columns):
720	        values = table._columns[i]
721	        payload, null_count, minimum, maximum = _encode_payload(
722	            col, values, use_dictionary=col.name in dict_set
723	        )
724	        chunk_info.append(
725	            {
726	                "name": col.name,
727	                "type": col.type,
728	                "nullable": col.nullable,
729	                "encoding": "dictionary" if col.name in dict_set else "plain",
730	                "offset": len(raw_section),
731	                "length": len(payload),
732	                "crc32": zlib.crc32(payload) & 0xFFFFFFFF,
733	                "null_count": null_count,
734	                "min": _stats_json(minimum),
735	                "max": _stats_json(maximum),
736	            }
737	        )
738	        raw_section.extend(payload)
739	
740	    if compression == "zlib":
741	        data_section = zlib.compress(bytes(raw_section), level=6)
742	    else:
743	        data_section = bytes(raw_section)
744	    header = _build_header(table, compression, data_section, bytes(raw_section), chunk_info)
745	    header_bytes = _dump_json(header)
746	    if len(header_bytes) > _MAX_HEADER_BYTES:
747	        raise ValueError("serialized header exceeds the size limit")
748	
749	    prefix = _MAGIC + bytes([FORMAT_VERSION]) + struct.pack("<I", len(header_bytes))
750	    body = prefix + header_bytes + data_section
751	    crc = zlib.crc32(body) & 0xFFFFFFFF
752	    blob = body + struct.pack("<I", crc) + _FOOTER_MARKER
753	
754	    _atomic_write(path, blob)
755	
756	
757	def _atomic_write(path: str | os.PathLike, blob: bytes) -> None:
758	    path = os.fspath(path)
759	    directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
760	    fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".columnar-", suffix=".tmp", dir=directory)
761	    try:
762	        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
763	            handle.write(blob)
764	            handle.flush()
765	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
766	        os.replace(tmp_name, path)
767	    except BaseException:
768	        try:
769	            os.unlink(tmp_name)
770	        except FileNotFoundError:
771	            pass
772	        raise

780	def _read_exact(handle, size: int, what: str) -> bytes:
781	    data = handle.read(size)
782	    if len(data) != size:
783	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"truncated file while reading {what}")
784	    return data
785	
786	
787	def _read_header(path: str | os.PathLike) -> tuple[bytes, bytes, dict, int]:
788	    """Read prefix + JSON header and fstat the declared total size.
789	
790	    Metadata-only: no data bytes are touched. Returns the raw prefix, raw
791	    header bytes, the validated header dict and the on-disk file size.
792	    """
793	    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
794	        prefix = handle.read(_PREFIX_LEN)
795	        if len(prefix) < _PREFIX_LEN:
796	            if not prefix:
797	                raise ColumnarFormatError("empty file")
798	            if len(prefix) >= 4 and prefix[:4] != _MAGIC:
799	                raise ColumnarFormatError("bad magic number")
800	            raise ColumnarFormatError("truncated file prefix")
801	        if prefix[:4] != _MAGIC:
802	            raise ColumnarFormatError("bad magic number")
803	        version = prefix[4]
804	        if version != FORMAT_VERSION:
805	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"unsupported format version: {version}")
806	        (header_length,) = struct.unpack("<I", prefix[5:9])
807	        if header_length == 0 or header_length > _MAX_HEADER_BYTES:
808	            raise ColumnarFormatError("header length out of bounds")
809	        header_bytes = _read_exact(handle, header_length, "header")
810	        actual_size = os.fstat(handle.fileno()).st_size
811	
812	    try:
813	        header = json.loads(
814	            header_bytes.decode("utf-8"),
815	            object_pairs_hook=_reject_duplicate_keys,
816	            parse_constant=_reject_json_constant,
817	        )
818	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
819	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"invalid header JSON: {exc}") from None
820	    header = _validate_header(header)
821	
822	    expected_size = _PREFIX_LEN + header_length + header["data_length"] + _FOOTER_LEN
823	    if actual_size != expected_size:
824	        raise ColumnarFormatError(
825	            f"file size {actual_size} does not match declared size {expected_size}"
826	        )
827	    return prefix, header_bytes, header, actual_size
828	
829	
830	def read_file(
831	    path: str | os.PathLike, *, columns: Sequence[str] | None = None
832	) -> Table:
833	    """Read a table, optionally projecting ``columns`` in the given order."""
834	    prefix, header_bytes, header, _ = _read_header(path)
835	    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
836	        handle.seek(_PREFIX_LEN + len(header_bytes))
837	        data_section = _read_exact(handle, header["data_length"], "data section")
838	        footer = _read_exact(handle, _FOOTER_LEN, "footer")
839	        if handle.read(1):
840	            raise ColumnarFormatError("trailing bytes after footer")
841	
842	    (footer_crc,) = struct.unpack("<I", footer[:4])
843	    if footer[4:] != _FOOTER_MARKER:
844	        raise ColumnarFormatError("bad end marker")
845	    covered = prefix + header_bytes + data_section
846	    if (zlib.crc32(covered) & 0xFFFFFFFF) != footer_crc:
847	        raise ColumnarFormatError("overall checksum mismatch")
848	    raw_section = _inflate(header, data_section)
849	
850	    schema_cols = []
851	    decoded_columns = []
852	    for entry in header["columns"]:
853	        col = ColumnSchema(entry["name"], entry["type"], entry["nullable"])
854	        schema_cols.append(col)
855	        start = entry["offset"]
856	        end = start + entry["length"]
857	        if end > len(raw_section):
858	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {col.name!r}: chunk outside data section")
859	        payload = raw_section[start:end]
860	        if (zlib.crc32(payload) & 0xFFFFFFFF) != entry["crc32"]:
861	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {col.name!r}: checksum mismatch")
862	        values = _decode_column(col, entry["encoding"], header["row_count"], payload)
863	        _verify_stats(col, values, entry)
864	        decoded_columns.append(values)
865	
866	    schema = Schema(schema_cols)
867	    table = Table._from_storage(schema, decoded_columns)
868	    if columns is not None:
869	        table = table.project(columns)
870	    return table
871	
872	
873	def _inflate(header: dict, data_section: bytes) -> bytes:
874	    if (zlib.crc32(data_section) & 0xFFFFFFFF) != header["data_crc32"]:
875	        raise ColumnarFormatError("data section checksum mismatch")
876	    if header["compression"] == "zlib":
877	        try:
878	            raw_section = zlib.decompress(data_section)
879	        except zlib.error as exc:
880	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"cannot decompress data section: {exc}") from None
881	    else:
882	        raw_section = data_section
883	    if len(raw_section) != header["uncompressed_length"]:
884	        raise ColumnarFormatError("uncompressed data length mismatch")
885	    return raw_section
886	
887	
888	def _verify_stats(col: ColumnSchema, values: Sequence, entry: dict) -> None:
889	    null_count = sum(1 for value in values if value is None)
890	    if null_count != entry["null_count"]:
891	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {col.name!r}: null_count mismatch")
892	    present = [value for value in values if value is not None]
893	    if not present:
894	        if entry["min"] is not None or entry["max"] is not None:
895	            raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {col.name!r}: stats mismatch")
896	        return
897	    minimum = min(present)
898	    maximum = max(present)
899	    meta_min = entry["min"]
900	    meta_max = entry["max"]
901	    if col.type == "float64":
902	        meta_min = float(meta_min)
903	        meta_max = float(meta_max)
904	    if minimum != meta_min or maximum != meta_max:
905	        raise ColumnarFormatError(f"column {col.name!r}: min/max mismatch")
906

908	def inspect_file(path: str | os.PathLike) -> dict:
909	    """Read only the file metadata; no data bytes are read, decompressed or decoded.
910	
911	    Returns a dict with fixed key order: ``format_version``, ``row_count``,
912	    ``columns``; columns stay in schema order, each with keys ``name``,

"""Tests for the two-file join query layer and the ``query-files`` CLI command."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json

import pytest

from columnar_analytics import (
    ColumnSchema,
    ColumnarFormatError,
    QuerySyntaxError,
    QueryValidationError,
    Schema,
    Table,
    query_file,
    query_files,
    write_file,
)
from columnar_analytics.cli import main


LEFT_SCHEMA = Schema(
    [
        ColumnSchema("id", "int64"),
        ColumnSchema("k", "int64", nullable=True),
        ColumnSchema("name", "utf8", nullable=True),
    ]
)
LEFT_DATA = {
    "id": [1, 2, 3, 4],
    "k": [10, 20, 10, None],
    "name": ["a", "b", "c", "d"],
}

RIGHT_SCHEMA = Schema(
    [
        ColumnSchema("rid", "int64"),
        ColumnSchema("k", "int64", nullable=True),
        ColumnSchema("tag", "utf8", nullable=True),
    ]
)
RIGHT_DATA = {
    "rid": [100, 200, 300],
    "k": [10, 10, 30],
    "tag": ["x", "y", "z"],
}


@pytest.fixture()
def paths(tmp_path):
    left = tmp_path / "left.caef"
    right = tmp_path / "right.caef"
    write_file(left, Table(LEFT_SCHEMA, LEFT_DATA))
    write_file(right, Table(RIGHT_SCHEMA, RIGHT_DATA))
    return {"l": left, "r": right}


def joined_rows(result):
    return [
        [result._columns[c][i] for c in range(len(result.schema.columns))]
        for i in range(result.row_count)
    ]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# INNER JOIN
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_inner_join_star(paths):
    result = query_files(paths, "SELECT * FROM l INNER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k")
    assert result.column_names == ("l.id", "l.k", "l.name", "r.rid", "r.k", "r.tag")
    # Left row order, right row order within one left row; NULL k never matches.
    assert joined_rows(result) == [
        [1, 10, "a", 100, 10, "x"],
        [1, 10, "a", 200, 10, "y"],
        [3, 10, "c", 100, 10, "x"],
        [3, 10, "c", 200, 10, "y"],
    ]
    # INNER JOIN keeps the right-side nullability from the file schema.
    assert [c.nullable for c in result.schema.columns] == [False, True, True, False, True, True]


def test_inner_join_projection_qualified_names(paths):
    result = query_files(paths, "SELECT r.tag, l.id FROM l INNER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k")
    assert result.column_names == ("r.tag", "l.id")
    assert result.column("l.id") == [1, 1, 3, 3]
    assert result.column("r.tag") == ["x", "y", "x", "y"]


def test_inner_join_where_order_limit(paths):
    result = query_files(
        paths,
        "SELECT l.id, r.rid FROM l INNER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k "
        "WHERE r.tag != 'x' ORDER BY l.id DESC LIMIT 1",
    )
    assert joined_rows(result) == [[3, 200]]


def test_join_aggregates(paths):
    result = query_files(
        paths,
        "SELECT l.name, COUNT(*), SUM(r.rid) FROM l INNER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k "
        "GROUP BY l.name ORDER BY l.name",
    )
    assert result.column_names == ("l.name", "COUNT(*)", "SUM(r.rid)")
    assert joined_rows(result) == [["a", 2, 300], ["c", 2, 300]]


def test_join_group_by_order_by_agg(paths):
    result = query_files(
        paths,
        "SELECT l.name, COUNT(*) FROM l INNER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k "
        "GROUP BY l.name ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC",
    )
    assert result.column("COUNT(*)") == [2, 2]


def test_left_join_unmatched_rows(paths):
    result = query_files(paths, "SELECT * FROM l LEFT JOIN r ON l.k = r.k")
    assert joined_rows(result) == [
        [1, 10, "a", 100, 10, "x"],
        [1, 10, "a", 200, 10, "y"],
        [2, 20, "b", None, None, None],
        [3, 10, "c", 100, 10, "x"],
        [3, 10, "c", 200, 10, "y"],
        [4, None, "d", None, None, None],
    ]
    # LEFT JOIN forces every right-side result column nullable.
    assert [c.nullable for c in result.schema.columns] == [False, True, True, True, True, True]


def test_left_join_explicit_projection_right_nullable(paths):
    result = query_files(paths, "SELECT l.id, r.tag FROM l LEFT JOIN r ON l.k = r.k")
    cols = {c.name: c for c in result.schema.columns}
    assert cols["l.id"].nullable is False
    assert cols["r.tag"].nullable is True


def test_right_join_star(paths):
    result = query_files(paths, "SELECT * FROM l RIGHT JOIN r ON l.k = r.k")
    assert result.column_names == ("l.id", "l.k", "l.name", "r.rid", "r.k", "r.tag")
    # Right-file order; within one right row the matches expand in left-file
    # order; the unmatched right row (rid 300) pads the left side with NULL.
    assert joined_rows(result) == [
        [1, 10, "a", 100, 10, "x"],
        [3, 10, "c", 100, 10, "x"],
        [1, 10, "a", 200, 10, "y"],
        [3, 10, "c", 200, 10, "y"],
        [None, None, None, 300, 30, "z"],
    ]
    # RIGHT JOIN forces every left-side result column nullable; the right
    # side keeps its file-declared nullability.
    assert [c.nullable for c in result.schema.columns] == [True, True, True, False, True, True]


def test_right_join_explicit_projection_left_nullable(paths):
    result = query_files(paths, "SELECT l.id, r.rid FROM l RIGHT JOIN r ON l.k = r.k")
    cols = {c.name: c for c in result.schema.columns}
    assert cols["l.id"].nullable is True
    assert cols["r.rid"].nullable is False
    assert joined_rows(result) == [
        [1, 100],
        [3, 100],
        [1, 200],
        [3, 200],
        [None, 300],
    ]


def test_full_outer_join_star(paths):
    result = query_files(paths, "SELECT * FROM l FULL OUTER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k")
    # Matches and unmatched left rows follow LEFT JOIN order; unmatched
    # right rows are then appended in right-file order.
    assert joined_rows(result) == [
        [1, 10, "a", 100, 10, "x"],
        [1, 10, "a", 200, 10, "y"],
        [2, 20, "b", None, None, None],
        [3, 10, "c", 100, 10, "x"],
        [3, 10, "c", 200, 10, "y"],
        [4, None, "d", None, None, None],
        [None, None, None, 300, 30, "z"],
    ]
    # FULL OUTER JOIN forces every result column on both sides nullable.
    assert [c.nullable for c in result.schema.columns] == [True, True, True, True, True, True]


def test_full_outer_join_keywords_case_insensitive(paths):
    result = query_files(paths, "select * from l full outer join r on l.k = r.k")
    assert result.row_count == 7


def test_right_join_where_order_limit(paths):
    result = query_files(
        paths,
        "SELECT l.id, r.rid FROM l RIGHT JOIN r ON l.k = r.k "
        "WHERE r.tag IS NOT NULL ORDER BY r.rid ASC, l.id ASC",
    )
    assert joined_rows(result) == [
        [1, 100],
        [3, 100],
        [1, 200],
        [3, 200],
        [None, 300],
    ]


def test_right_join_padded_null_participates_in_where(paths):
    # The padded NULL on the left follows three-valued logic in WHERE.
    result = query_files(
        paths,
        "SELECT r.rid FROM l RIGHT JOIN r ON l.k = r.k WHERE l.id IS NULL",
    )
    assert joined_rows(result) == [[300]]
    result = query_files(
        paths,
        "SELECT r.rid FROM l RIGHT JOIN r ON l.k = r.k WHERE l.id = 1",
    )
    assert joined_rows(result) == [[100], [200]]


def test_full_outer_join_aggregates(paths):
    result = query_files(
        paths,
        "SELECT l.name, COUNT(*), SUM(r.rid) FROM l FULL OUTER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k "
        "GROUP BY l.name ORDER BY l.name",
    )
    # The unmatched right row forms a NULL-keyed group; COUNT(*) counts it,
    # SUM skips no rid there since the right side is populated; unmatched
    # left rows (name b, d) form their own groups with SUM(r.rid) NULL.
    assert joined_rows(result) == [
        ["a", 2, 300],
        ["b", 1, None],
        ["c", 2, 300],
        ["d", 1, None],
        [None, 1, 300],
    ]


def test_full_outer_join_distinct_and_order(paths):
    result = query_files(
        paths,
        "SELECT DISTINCT l.k, r.k FROM l FULL OUTER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k "
        "ORDER BY l.k NULLS LAST, r.k NULLS LAST",
    )
    # Padded NULLs on either side compare equal in DISTINCT; rk NULLS LAST
    # keeps (None, None) behind (None, 30) inside the NULL l.k group.
    assert joined_rows(result) == [
        [10, 10],
        [20, None],
        [None, 30],
        [None, None],
    ]


def test_right_and_full_duplicate_keys_full_combination(tmp_path):
    left = tmp_path / "dl.caef"
    right = tmp_path / "dr.caef"
    write_file(left, Table(Schema([ColumnSchema("k", "int64")]), {"k": [1, 1, 2]}))
    write_file(right, Table(Schema([ColumnSchema("k", "int64")]), {"k": [1, 1, 3]}))
    sources = {"a": left, "b": right}
    right_rows = joined_rows(
        query_files(sources, "SELECT * FROM a RIGHT JOIN b ON a.k = b.k")
    )
    assert right_rows == [
        [1, 1], [1, 1], [1, 1], [1, 1],
        [None, 3],
    ]
    full_rows = joined_rows(
        query_files(sources, "SELECT * FROM a FULL OUTER JOIN b ON a.k = b.k")
    )
    assert full_rows == [
        [1, 1], [1, 1], [1, 1], [1, 1],
        [2, None],
        [None, 3],
    ]


def test_null_keys_never_match_right_and_full(tmp_path):
    left = tmp_path / "nl.caef"
    right = tmp_path / "nr.caef"
    write_file(left, Table(Schema([ColumnSchema("k", "int64", nullable=True)]), {"k": [None, 1]}))
    write_file(right, Table(Schema([ColumnSchema("k", "int64", nullable=True)]), {"k": [None, 2]}))
    sources = {"a": left, "b": right}
    assert joined_rows(query_files(sources, "SELECT * FROM a RIGHT JOIN b ON a.k = b.k")) == [
        [None, None],
        [None, 2],
    ]
    assert joined_rows(query_files(sources, "SELECT * FROM a FULL OUTER JOIN b ON a.k = b.k")) == [
        [None, None],
        [1, None],
        [None, None],
        [None, 2],
    ]


def test_join_keywords_case_insensitive_and_quoted(paths):
    result = query_files(paths, 'select "l"."id" from "l" inner join "r" on "l"."k" = "r"."k"')
    assert result.column_names == ("l.id",)
    assert result.column("l.id") == [1, 1, 3, 3]


def test_join_int64_float64_keys(tmp_path):
    left = tmp_path / "li.caef"
    right = tmp_path / "rf.caef"
    write_file(left, Table(Schema([ColumnSchema("k", "int64")]), {"k": [1, 2]}))
    write_file(right, Table(Schema([ColumnSchema("k", "float64")]), {"k": [2.0, 3.0]}))
    result = query_files(
        {"a": left, "b": right}, "SELECT a.k, b.k FROM a INNER JOIN b ON a.k = b.k"
    )
    assert joined_rows(result) == [[2, 2.0]]


def test_join_utf8_keys(tmp_path):
    left = tmp_path / "lu.caef"
    right = tmp_path / "ru.caef"
    write_file(left, Table(Schema([ColumnSchema("k", "utf8")]), {"k": ["x", "y"]}))
    write_file(right, Table(Schema([ColumnSchema("k", "utf8")]), {"k": ["y"]}))
    result = query_files(
        {"a": left, "b": right}, "SELECT a.k FROM a INNER JOIN b ON a.k = b.k"
    )
    assert result.column("a.k") == ["y"]


def test_query_files_single_table_no_join(paths):
    result = query_files(paths, "SELECT id, name FROM l WHERE id >= 2 ORDER BY id")
    assert result.column_names == ("id", "name")
    assert result.column("id") == [2, 3, 4]


def test_query_files_single_table_qualified(paths):
    result = query_files(paths, "SELECT l.id FROM l WHERE l.id = 1")
    assert result.column_names == ("id",)
    assert result.column("id") == [1]


def test_query_files_unreferenced_source_not_read(tmp_path):
    left = tmp_path / "left.caef"
    write_file(left, Table(LEFT_SCHEMA, LEFT_DATA))
    sources = {"l": left, "missing": tmp_path / "does-not-exist.caef"}
    result = query_files(sources, "SELECT id FROM l WHERE id = 1")
    assert result.column("id") == [1]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Syntax errors (raised before any file is read)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql",
    [
        "SELECT * FROM l JOIN r ON l.k = r.k",                # missing INNER/LEFT/...
        "SELECT * FROM l CROSS JOIN r ON l.k = r.k",          # unsupported join type
        "SELECT * FROM l FULL JOIN r ON l.k = r.k",           # FULL without OUTER
        "SELECT * FROM l FULL OUTER r ON l.k = r.k",          # missing JOIN
        "SELECT * FROM l RIGHT OUTER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k",    # RIGHT takes no OUTER
        "SELECT * FROM l LEFT OUTER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k",     # LEFT takes no OUTER
        "SELECT * FROM l FULL OUTER JOIN r",                  # missing ON
        "SELECT * FROM l INNER r ON l.k = r.k",               # missing JOIN
        "SELECT * FROM l INNER JOIN r",                       # missing ON
        "SELECT * FROM l INNER JOIN r ON l.k",                # incomplete ON
        "SELECT * FROM l INNER JOIN r ON l.k > r.k",          # non-equality ON
        "SELECT * FROM l INNER JOIN r ON k = r.k",            # unqualified ON key
        "SELECT * FROM l INNER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k AND l.id = 1",  # compound ON
        "SELECT * FROM l INNER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k INNER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k",  # two joins
        "SELECT * FROM l INNER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k LEFT JOIN r ON l.k = r.k",
        "SELECT * FROM l x INNER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k",        # alias
    ],
)
def test_join_syntax_errors_before_file_access(sql):
    missing = {"l": "/nonexistent/l.caef", "r": "/nonexistent/r.caef"}
    with pytest.raises(QuerySyntaxError):
        query_files(missing, sql)


def test_query_file_still_rejects_join(paths):
    with pytest.raises(QuerySyntaxError):
        query_file(paths["l"], "SELECT * FROM input INNER JOIN r ON input.k = r.k")


def test_query_file_still_rejects_qualified(paths):
    with pytest.raises(QuerySyntaxError):
        query_file(paths["l"], "SELECT input.id FROM input")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Validation errors
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_unknown_from_table(paths):
    with pytest.raises(QueryValidationError):
        query_files(paths, "SELECT * FROM nope")


def test_unknown_join_table(paths):
    with pytest.raises(QueryValidationError):
        query_files(paths, "SELECT * FROM l INNER JOIN nope ON l.k = nope.k")


def test_duplicate_table(paths):
    with pytest.raises(QueryValidationError):
        query_files(paths, "SELECT * FROM l INNER JOIN l ON l.k = l.k")


def test_unqualified_column_in_join(paths):
    with pytest.raises(QueryValidationError):
        query_files(paths, "SELECT id FROM l INNER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k")


def test_unqualified_column_in_join_where(paths):
    with pytest.raises(QueryValidationError):
        query_files(paths, "SELECT l.id FROM l INNER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k WHERE id = 1")


def test_unknown_column_in_join(paths):
    with pytest.raises(QueryValidationError):
        query_files(paths, "SELECT l.nope FROM l INNER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k")


def test_unknown_table_qualifier(paths):
    with pytest.raises(QueryValidationError):
        query_files(paths, "SELECT z.id FROM l INNER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k")


def test_on_key_from_wrong_side(paths):
    with pytest.raises(QueryValidationError):
        query_files(paths, "SELECT * FROM l INNER JOIN r ON r.k = l.k")


def test_on_key_same_table(paths):
    with pytest.raises(QueryValidationError):
        query_files(paths, "SELECT * FROM l INNER JOIN r ON l.k = l.id")


def test_on_unknown_key_column(paths):
    with pytest.raises(QueryValidationError):
        query_files(paths, "SELECT * FROM l INNER JOIN r ON l.nope = r.k")


def test_incompatible_key_types(tmp_path):
    left = tmp_path / "a.caef"
    right = tmp_path / "b.caef"
    write_file(left, Table(Schema([ColumnSchema("k", "utf8")]), {"k": ["x"]}))
    write_file(right, Table(Schema([ColumnSchema("k", "int64")]), {"k": [1]}))
    with pytest.raises(QueryValidationError):
        query_files({"a": left, "b": right}, "SELECT * FROM a INNER JOIN b ON a.k = b.k")


def test_duplicate_result_column(paths):
    with pytest.raises(QueryValidationError):
        query_files(paths, "SELECT l.id, l.id FROM l INNER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k")


def test_duplicate_result_column_case_variant(paths):
    with pytest.raises(QueryValidationError):
        query_files(paths, "SELECT L.id, l.id FROM l INNER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# sources validation (ValueError, no file access)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sources",
    [
        "not-a-mapping",
        42,
        {},
        {"": "x.caef"},
        {1: "x.caef"},
        {"t": 123},
        {"t": None},
    ],
)
def test_invalid_sources_value_error(sources):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        query_files(sources, "SELECT * FROM t")


def test_invalid_sources_no_file_access():
    # An invalid key must raise ValueError before the (nonexistent) path is
    # ever touched -- an OSError here would prove a file access happened.
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        query_files({"": "/nonexistent/x.caef"}, "SELECT * FROM t")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        query_files({"t": 123}, "SELECT * FROM t")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# File errors
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_missing_file_oserror(tmp_path):

def test_corrupt_referenced_file(paths, tmp_path):
    bad = tmp_path / "bad.caef"
    bad.write_bytes(b"garbage")
    with pytest.raises(ColumnarFormatError):
        query_files({"l": paths["l"], "r": bad}, "SELECT * FROM l INNER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CLI
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_cli_query_files_success(paths, capsys):
    sources_json = json.dumps({"l": str(paths["l"]), "r": str(paths["r"])})
    sql = "SELECT l.id, r.tag FROM l LEFT JOIN r ON l.k = r.k"
    assert main(["query-files", sources_json, sql]) == 0
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    payload = json.loads(out)
    assert list(payload) == ["columns", "rows"]
    assert [c["name"] for c in payload["columns"]] == ["l.id", "r.tag"]
    assert payload["columns"][1]["nullable"] is True
    assert payload["rows"] == [
        [1, "x"],
        [1, "y"],
        [2, None],
        [3, "x"],
        [3, "y"],
        [4, None],
    ]
    # Byte-identical across runs without explicit ORDER BY.
    assert main(["query-files", sources_json, sql]) == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out == out


def test_cli_query_files_bad_sql_exit_2(paths, capsys):
    sources_json = json.dumps({"l": str(paths["l"]), "r": str(paths["r"])})
    assert main(["query-files", sources_json, "SELECT * FROM l JOIN r"]) == 2
    assert capsys.readouterr().err


def test_cli_query_files_invalid_sources_json_exit_2(capsys):
    assert main(["query-files", "{not json", "SELECT * FROM l"]) == 2
    assert capsys.readouterr().err


def test_cli_query_files_bad_sources_shape_exit_2(capsys):
    assert main(["query-files", "[]", "SELECT * FROM l"]) == 2
    assert capsys.readouterr().err


def test_cli_query_files_missing_file_exit_1(tmp_path, capsys):
    sources_json = json.dumps({"l": str(tmp_path / "nope.caef")})
    assert main(["query-files", sources_json, "SELECT * FROM l"]) == 1
    assert capsys.readouterr().err


def test_cli_query_still_works(paths, capsys):
    rc = main(["query", str(paths["l"]), "SELECT id FROM input WHERE id = 1"])
    assert rc == 0
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert json.loads(out)["rows"] == [[1]]

399	    p.write_bytes(body + struct.pack("<I", zlib.crc32(body) & 0xFFFFFFFF) + b"END1")

"""Tests for the metadata-only explain layer and the explain CLI commands."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import struct
import zlib

import pytest

from columnar_analytics import (
    ColumnSchema,
    ColumnarFormatError,
    QuerySyntaxError,
    QueryValidationError,
    Schema,
    Table,
    explain_file,
    explain_files,
    query_file,
    query_files,
    read_file,
    write_file,
)
from columnar_analytics.cli import main


SCHEMA = Schema(
    [
        ColumnSchema("id", "int64"),
        ColumnSchema("n", "int64", nullable=True),
        ColumnSchema("f", "float64", nullable=True),

def test_filter_condition_recursive_tree(path):
    plan = explain_file(
        path,
        "SELECT id FROM input WHERE NOT (n <= 10 AND s = 'a') OR flag IS NULL",
    )
    cond = find_operator(plan, "Filter")["condition"]
    assert cond["kind"] == "logic"
    assert cond["operator"] == "OR"
    left, right = cond["operands"]
    assert left["kind"] == "not"
    and_node = left["operands"][0]
    assert and_node["kind"] == "logic"
    assert and_node["operator"] == "AND"
    cmp_node = and_node["operands"][0]
    assert cmp_node["kind"] == "comparison"
    assert cmp_node["operator"] == "<="
    assert cmp_node["operands"][0] == {"kind": "column", "name": "n"}
    assert cmp_node["operands"][1] == {"kind": "literal", "type": "int64", "value": 10}
    assert right["kind"] == "is_null"
    assert right["operator"] == "IS NULL"
    assert right["operands"][0] == {"kind": "column", "name": "flag"}


def test_filter_typed_literals(path):

        ("n = -9223372036854775808", "int64", -(2**63)),

    for sql_suffix, type_name, value in cases:
        plan = explain_file(path, f"SELECT id FROM input WHERE {sql_suffix}")

def test_join_plan_shape(sources):
    sql = (
        "SELECT l.id, r.tag, COUNT(*) FROM l INNER JOIN r ON l.id = r.k "
        "WHERE l.s IS NOT NULL GROUP BY l.id, r.tag ORDER BY l.id LIMIT 5"

    plan = explain_files(sources, sql)
    assert [s["name"] for s in plan["sources"]] == ["l", "r"]
    assert plan["sources"][0]["row_count"] == 5

    assert kinds == [
        "Scan",
        "Scan",
        "Join",
        "Filter",
        "Aggregate",
        "Sort",
        "Limit",

    scans = [op for op in plan["operators"] if op["operator"] == "Scan"]

    assert scans == {"l": ["n"], "r": ["k"]}
    assert find_operator(plan, "Join")["type"] == "LEFT"

    star = explain_files(sources, "SELECT * FROM l LEFT JOIN r ON l.id = r.k")

def test_explain_ignores_footer_crc_but_read_fails(path):
    raw = path.read_bytes()
    # Flip one byte of the final overall CRC checksum; size stays identical.
    path.write_bytes(raw[:-5] + bytes([raw[-5] ^ 0xFF]) + raw[-4:])
    plan = explain_file(path, "SELECT id FROM input")
    assert plan["output"][0]["name"] == "id"
    with pytest.raises(ColumnarFormatError):
        read_file(path)


def test_explain_ignores_value_level_stats_corruption(tmp_path):
    p = tmp_path / "plain.caef"
    schema = Schema([ColumnSchema("id", "int64")])
    write_file(p, Table(schema, {"id": [42]}))
    raw = p.read_bytes()
    header_len = struct.unpack("<I", raw[5:9])[0]
    header = json.loads(raw[9 : 9 + header_len].decode("utf-8"))
    data = bytearray(raw[9 + header_len : -8])
    data[0] ^= 0x01  # perturb the int64 payload -> min/max stats now wrong
    header["data_crc32"] = zlib.crc32(bytes(data)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    header_bytes = json.dumps(header, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
    body = raw[:4] + bytes([1]) + struct.pack("<I", len(header_bytes)) + header_bytes + bytes(data)
    p.write_bytes(body + struct.pack("<I", zlib.crc32(body) & 0xFFFFFFFF) + b"END1")
    plan = explain_file(p, "SELECT id FROM input")
    assert plan["sources"][0]["row_count"] == 1
    with pytest.raises(ColumnarFormatError):
        read_file(p)

"""Tests for the optional ``join_strategy`` argument (hash / sort_merge).

The two strategies must return identical column descriptions, values,
NULL positions and row order; only the explain plan distinguishes them,
and only when a strategy was requested explicitly.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json

import pytest

from columnar_analytics import (
    ColumnSchema,
    Schema,
    Table,
    explain_files,
    export_query_files,
    query_files,
    write_file,
)
from columnar_analytics.cli import main


def joined_rows(result):
    return [
        [result._columns[c][i] for c in range(len(result.schema.columns))]
        for i in range(result.row_count)
    ]


def schema_dicts(table):
    return [
        {"name": col.name, "type": col.type, "nullable": col.nullable}
        for col in table.schema.columns
    ]


@pytest.fixture()
def paths(tmp_path):
    # Duplicate keys (10 appears twice on each side), NULL keys and an
    # unmatched value on both sides exercise every join edge case.
    left = tmp_path / "left.caef"
    right = tmp_path / "right.caef"
    write_file(
        left,
        Table(
            Schema(
                [
                    ColumnSchema("id", "int64"),
                    ColumnSchema("k", "int64", nullable=True),
                    ColumnSchema("name", "utf8", nullable=True),
                ]
            ),
            {
                "id": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5],
                "k": [10, 20, 10, None, 30],
                "name": ["a", "b", "c", "d", "e"],
            },
        ),
    )
    write_file(
        right,
        Table(
            Schema(
                [
                    ColumnSchema("rid", "int64"),
                    ColumnSchema("k", "int64", nullable=True),
                    ColumnSchema("tag", "utf8", nullable=True),
                ]
            ),
            {
                "rid": [100, 200, 300, 400, 500],
                "k": [30, 10, None, 10, 20],
                "tag": ["p", "q", None, "r", "s"],
            },
        ),
    )
    return {"l": left, "r": right}


JOIN_SQL = [
    "SELECT * FROM l INNER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k",
    "SELECT * FROM l LEFT JOIN r ON l.k = r.k",
    "SELECT * FROM l RIGHT JOIN r ON l.k = r.k",
    "SELECT * FROM l FULL OUTER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k",
    "SELECT l.id, r.rid FROM l INNER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k "
    "WHERE r.tag IS NOT NULL ORDER BY l.id DESC, r.rid ASC LIMIT 3",
    "SELECT l.name, COUNT(*), SUM(r.rid) FROM l LEFT JOIN r ON l.k = r.k "
    "GROUP BY l.name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1 ORDER BY l.name",
    "SELECT l.id, r.rid, l.k + r.k AS s FROM l INNER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k "
    "WHERE l.k + r.k > 15 ORDER BY s",
    "SELECT l.id, r.rid FROM l RIGHT JOIN r ON l.k = r.k "
    "WHERE l.id IS NULL OR r.tag IS NULL ORDER BY r.rid",
    "SELECT l.id, r.rid FROM l FULL OUTER JOIN r ON l.k = r.k "
    "ORDER BY r.rid NULLS FIRST, l.id NULLS FIRST LIMIT 4",
]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("sql", JOIN_SQL)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("strategy", ["hash", "sort_merge"])
def test_strategies_match_default_path(paths, sql, strategy):
    default = query_files(paths, sql)
    chosen = query_files(paths, sql, strategy)
    assert schema_dicts(chosen) == schema_dicts(default)
    assert joined_rows(chosen) == joined_rows(default)


def test_strategies_match_each_other_all_kinds(paths):
    expected_inner = [
        # Left file order; within one left row the right matches follow the
        # right file's original order (rid 200 before 400 for key 10).
        [1, 10, "a", 200, 10, "q"],
        [1, 10, "a", 400, 10, "r"],
        [2, 20, "b", 500, 20, "s"],
        [3, 10, "c", 200, 10, "q"],
        [3, 10, "c", 400, 10, "r"],
        [5, 30, "e", 100, 30, "p"],
    ]
    # The unmatched NULL-keyed left row (id 4) keeps its original position
    # between ids 3 and 5.
    expected_left = expected_inner[:5] + [
        [4, None, "d", None, None, None],
        expected_inner[5],
    ]
    # RIGHT follows right-file order (rid 100/30/500 first) with each right
    # row's matches in left-file order; the NULL-keyed right row (rid 300)
    # and the key-20-only right row (rid 500) keep their file positions.
    expected_right = [
        [5, 30, "e", 100, 30, "p"],
        [1, 10, "a", 200, 10, "q"],
        [3, 10, "c", 200, 10, "q"],
        [None, None, None, 300, None, None],
        [1, 10, "a", 400, 10, "r"],
        [3, 10, "c", 400, 10, "r"],
        [2, 20, "b", 500, 20, "s"],
    ]
    # FULL is the LEFT output followed by the unmatched right rows (only the
    # NULL-keyed rid 300) in right-file order.
    expected_full = expected_left + [
        [None, None, None, 300, None, None],
    ]
    for kind, spelling, expected in (
        ("INNER", "INNER", expected_inner),
        ("LEFT", "LEFT", expected_left),
        ("RIGHT", "RIGHT", expected_right),
        ("FULL", "FULL OUTER", expected_full),
    ):
        sql = f"SELECT * FROM l {spelling} JOIN r ON l.k = r.k"
        default_rows = joined_rows(query_files(paths, sql))
        hash_rows = joined_rows(query_files(paths, sql, "hash"))
        merge_rows = joined_rows(query_files(paths, sql, "sort_merge"))
        assert default_rows == expected, kind
        assert hash_rows == expected, kind
        assert merge_rows == expected, kind


def test_int64_float64_mixed_keys_and_signed_zero(tmp_path):
    left = tmp_path / "li.caef"
    right = tmp_path / "rf.caef"
    write_file(
        left,
        Table(Schema([ColumnSchema("k", "int64")]), {"k": [0, 1, 2, 2, 3]}),
    )
    write_file(
        right,
        Table(
            Schema([ColumnSchema("k", "float64", nullable=True)]),
            {"k": [2.0, -0.0, 2.0, None, 1.0]},
        ),
    )
    sql = "SELECT a.k, b.k FROM a INNER JOIN b ON a.k = b.k"
    sources = {"a": left, "b": right}
    expected = [
        # +0 and -0 match; duplicate keys produce the full combination set
        # in left order / right order regardless of strategy.
        [0, -0.0],
        [1, 1.0],
        [2, 2.0],
        [2, 2.0],
        [2, 2.0],
        [2, 2.0],
    ]
    assert joined_rows(query_files(sources, sql, "hash")) == expected
    assert joined_rows(query_files(sources, sql, "sort_merge")) == expected


def test_utf8_keys_equivalence(tmp_path):
    left = tmp_path / "lu.caef"
    right = tmp_path / "ru.caef"
    write_file(
        left,
        Table(
            Schema([ColumnSchema("k", "utf8", nullable=True)]),
            {"k": ["x", "y", "y", None, "z"]},
        ),
    )
    write_file(
        right,
        Table(
            Schema([ColumnSchema("k", "utf8", nullable=True)]),
            {"k": ["y", "x", "y", "w", None]},
        ),
    )
    sql = "SELECT a.k, b.k FROM a LEFT JOIN b ON a.k = b.k"
    sources = {"a": left, "b": right}
    expected = [
        ["x", "x"],
        ["y", "y"],
        ["y", "y"],
        ["y", "y"],
        ["y", "y"],
        [None, None],
        ["z", None],

"""Tests for the CSV / JSONL query-export layer and the export CLI commands."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json

import pytest

from columnar_analytics import (
    ColumnSchema,
    ColumnarFormatError,
    QuerySyntaxError,
    QueryValidationError,
    Schema,
    Table,
    export_query_file,
    export_query_files,
    write_file,
)
from columnar_analytics.cli import main

SCHEMA = Schema(
    [
        ColumnSchema("id", "int64"),
        ColumnSchema("n", "int64", nullable=True),
        ColumnSchema("f", "float64", nullable=True),
        ColumnSchema("s", "utf8", nullable=True),
        ColumnSchema("flag", "bool"),
        ColumnSchema("名前", "utf8", nullable=True),
    ]
)

DATA = {
    "id": [1, 2, 3],
    "n": [10, None, 30],
    "f": [1.5, None, -0.0],
    "s": ["plain", "", 'a,b"x"\ny'],
    "flag": [True, False, True],
    "名前": ["い", None, "ろ"],
}


@pytest.fixture()
def path(tmp_path):
    p = tmp_path / "t.caef"
    write_file(p, Table(SCHEMA, DATA))
    return p


def read_bytes(path):
    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
        return handle.read()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CSV
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_csv_default_format_header_order_and_lf(path, tmp_path):
    dst = tmp_path / "out.csv"
    rows = export_query_file(path, "SELECT id, n, f, s, flag FROM input ORDER BY id", dst)
    assert rows == 3
    blob = read_bytes(dst)
    assert not blob.startswith(b"\xef\xbb\xbf")  # no UTF-8 BOM
    assert blob == (
        b"id,n,f,s,flag\n"
        b"1,10,1.5,plain,true\n"
        b"2,,,\"\",false\n"
        b'3,30,-0.0,"a,b""x""\ny",true\n'
    )
    assert b"\r" not in blob
    assert blob.endswith(b"\n")


def test_csv_null_is_empty_field_empty_string_is_quoted(path, tmp_path):
    dst = tmp_path / "out.csv"
    export_query_file(
        path, "SELECT s, n FROM input WHERE id = 1 OR id = 2 ORDER BY id", dst
    )
    lines = read_bytes(dst).decode("utf-8").split("\n")
    assert lines == ["s,n", "plain,10", '"",', ""]


def test_csv_quoting_rules_and_quote_doubling(path, tmp_path):
    dst = tmp_path / "out.csv"
    export_query_file(path, "SELECT s FROM input WHERE id = 3", dst)
    text = read_bytes(dst).decode("utf-8")
    assert text == 's\n"a,b""x""\ny"\n'


def test_csv_carriage_return_is_quoted_and_preserved(tmp_path):
    schema = Schema([ColumnSchema("v", "utf8")])
    p = tmp_path / "cr.caef"
    write_file(p, Table(schema, {"v": ["a\rb"]}))
    dst = tmp_path / "out.csv"
    export_query_file(p, "SELECT v FROM input", dst)
    assert read_bytes(dst) == b'v\n"a\rb"\n'


def test_csv_bool_and_number_text(path, tmp_path):
    dst = tmp_path / "out.csv"
    export_query_file(path, "SELECT flag, f, id FROM input WHERE id = 1", dst)
    assert read_bytes(dst) == b"flag,f,id\ntrue,1.5,1\n"


def test_csv_non_ascii_is_not_escaped(path, tmp_path):
    dst = tmp_path / "out.csv"
    export_query_file(path, "SELECT 名前 FROM input WHERE id = 1", dst)
    assert read_bytes(dst) == "名前\nい\n".encode("utf-8")


def test_csv_zero_rows_is_header_only(path, tmp_path):
    dst = tmp_path / "out.csv"
    rows = export_query_file(path, "SELECT id, s FROM input WHERE id > 1000", dst)
    assert rows == 0
    assert read_bytes(dst) == b"id,s\n"


def test_csv_header_escapes_special_characters(tmp_path):
    schema = Schema(
        [ColumnSchema("a,b", "int64"), ColumnSchema('q"q', "utf8", nullable=True)]
    )
    p = tmp_path / "weird.caef"
    write_file(p, Table(schema, {"a,b": [1], 'q"q': ["x"]}))
    dst = tmp_path / "out.csv"
    export_query_file(p, "SELECT * FROM input", dst)
    assert read_bytes(dst) == b'"a,b","q""q"\n1,x\n'


def test_csv_aggregate_and_scalar_alias_labels(path, tmp_path):
    agg = tmp_path / "agg.csv"
    export_query_file(
        path,
        "SELECT flag, COUNT(*) FROM input GROUP BY flag ORDER BY flag",
        agg,
    )
    lines = read_bytes(agg).decode("utf-8").split("\n")
    assert lines[0] == "flag,COUNT(*)"
    assert lines[1] == "false,1"
    assert lines[2] == "true,2"
    assert lines[3] == ""

    expr = tmp_path / "expr.csv"
    export_query_file(
        path, "SELECT id + 1 AS next FROM input WHERE id = 1", expr
    )
    assert read_bytes(expr) == b"next\n2\n"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# JSONL
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_jsonl_compact_objects_in_column_order(path, tmp_path):
    dst = tmp_path / "out.jsonl"
    rows = export_query_file(
        path,
        "SELECT id, n, f, s, flag FROM input ORDER BY id",
        dst,
        format="jsonl",
    )
    assert rows == 3
    blob = read_bytes(dst)
    assert blob == (
        b'{"id":1,"n":10,"f":1.5,"s":"plain","flag":true}\n'
        b'{"id":2,"n":null,"f":null,"s":"","flag":false}\n'
        b'{"id":3,"n":30,"f":-0.0,"s":"a,b\\"x\\"\\ny","flag":true}\n'
    )
    for line in blob.decode("utf-8").splitlines():
        json.loads(line)  # every line is a standalone JSON object


def test_jsonl_non_ascii_unescaped_and_null(path, tmp_path):
    dst = tmp_path / "out.jsonl"
    export_query_file(
        path, "SELECT 名前 FROM input ORDER BY id", dst, format="jsonl"
    )
    blob = read_bytes(dst)
    assert blob == '{"名前":"い"}\n{"名前":null}\n{"名前":"ろ"}\n'.encode("utf-8")
    assert b"\\u" not in blob


def test_jsonl_zero_rows_is_zero_bytes(path, tmp_path):
    dst = tmp_path / "out.jsonl"
    rows = export_query_file(
        path, "SELECT id FROM input WHERE id > 1000", dst, format="jsonl"
    )
    assert rows == 0
    assert read_bytes(dst) == b""


def test_jsonl_join_qualified_keys(tmp_path):
    left = tmp_path / "l.caef"
    right = tmp_path / "r.caef"
    write_file(
        left,
        Table(
            Schema([ColumnSchema("id", "int64"), ColumnSchema("v", "utf8")]),
            {"id": [1], "v": ["x"]},
        ),
    )
    write_file(
        right,
        Table(
            Schema([ColumnSchema("id", "int64"), ColumnSchema("tag", "utf8")]),
            {"id": [1], "tag": ["y"]},
        ),
    )
    dst = tmp_path / "out.jsonl"
    export_query_files(
        {"l": left, "r": right},
        "SELECT l.id, r.tag FROM l INNER JOIN r ON l.id = r.id",
        dst,
        format="jsonl",
    )
    blob = read_bytes(dst)
    assert blob == b'{"l.id":1,"r.tag":"y"}\n'
    assert list(json.loads(blob.decode("utf-8").strip()).keys()) == ["l.id", "r.tag"]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Determinism
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_repeated_exports_are_byte_identical(path, tmp_path):
    a = tmp_path / "a.csv"
    b = tmp_path / "b.csv"
    export_query_file(path, "SELECT id, s FROM input", a)
    export_query_file(path, "SELECT id, s FROM input", b)
    assert read_bytes(a) == read_bytes(b)

    aj = tmp_path / "a.jsonl"
    bj = tmp_path / "bj.jsonl"
    export_query_file(path, "SELECT id, s FROM input", aj, format="jsonl")
    export_query_file(path, "SELECT id, s FROM input", bj, format="jsonl")
    assert read_bytes(aj) == read_bytes(bj)


def test_export_without_order_by_keeps_deterministic_query_order(path, tmp_path):
    first = tmp_path / "first.csv"
    second = tmp_path / "second.csv"
    sql = "SELECT s FROM input WHERE id >= 2"
    export_query_file(path, sql, first)
    export_query_file(path, sql, second)
    assert read_bytes(first) == read_bytes(second)
    assert read_bytes(first) == b's\n""\n"a,b""x""\ny"\n'


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Argument validation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_unknown_format_raises_value_error(path, tmp_path):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        export_query_file(path, "SELECT id FROM input", tmp_path / "x", format="xml")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        export_query_file(path, "SELECT id FROM input", tmp_path / "x", format=None)


def test_destination_aliasing_source_raises_value_error(path, tmp_path):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        export_query_file(path, "SELECT id FROM input", path)
    # The overlap check precedes query execution: a syntactically invalid
    # statement still raises ValueError for the alias.
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        export_query_file(path, "NOT SQL", path)
    assert path.exists()


def test_destination_aliasing_source_via_relative_or_symlink(path, tmp_path):
    import os

    alias = tmp_path / "alias.caef"
    os.symlink(path, alias)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        export_query_file(path, "SELECT id FROM input", alias)

    # A destination spelling the same file through "." / ".." still aliases.
    cwd = os.getcwd()
    try:
        os.chdir(tmp_path)
        rel = os.path.join(".", os.path.basename(path))
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            export_query_file(rel, "SELECT id FROM input", rel)
    finally:
        os.chdir(cwd)


def test_destination_aliasing_referenced_join_source(tmp_path):
    left = tmp_path / "l.caef"
    right = tmp_path / "r.caef"
    one_row = Table(Schema([ColumnSchema("id", "int64")]), {"id": [1]})
    write_file(left, one_row)
    write_file(right, one_row)
    sources = {"l": left, "r": right}
    sql = "SELECT l.id FROM l INNER JOIN r ON l.id = r.id"
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        export_query_files(sources, sql, left)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        export_query_files(sources, sql, right)
    # An unreferenced source may be overwritten by the export.
    only_left = tmp_path / "only.csv"
    export_query_files({"l": left, "r": right}, "SELECT id FROM l", only_left)
    assert read_bytes(only_left) == b"id\n1\n"


def test_sources_validation_still_value_error(tmp_path):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        export_query_files({}, "SELECT id FROM l", tmp_path / "x")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_syntax_error_creates_no_destination(path, tmp_path):

            str(right),
